summary: Dallas/Fort Worth's two largest commercial sectors continued to diverge in Q1 2026, with the industrial market substantially outpacing office on both demand and momentum. Industrial recorded 4.3 million s.f. of year-to-date net absorption against 18.5 million s.f. of leasing activity, holding vacancy at 8.3% with asking rents at $8.71 psf NNN, while office posted just 117,000 s.f. of net absorption on 3.3 million s.f. of leasing and an elevated 24.5% vacancy rate. Despite that high vacancy, office asking rents remained firm at $34.04 psf overall and $39.90 psf for Class A, with both expected to rise as vacancy is forecast to decline. The development pipeline underscores the gap in conviction, as industrial has 31.2 million s.f. under construction compared with roughly 2.0 million s.f. for office, reflecting sustained logistics-driven demand across the metro.
